target.name: anti-Mullerian hormone receptor signaling pathway
target.description: Anti-Mullerian hormone signalling is how the fetal testis eliminates the precursor of the female reproductive tract: Sertoli-cell-derived AMH acting through its dedicated type II receptor drives regression of the Mullerian ducts, and loss of either the hormone or AMHR2 leaves genetically male individuals with a uterus and fallopian tubes, the persistent Mullerian duct syndrome. The same axis continues after development, restraining recruitment of primordial ovarian follicles and serving as a circulating index of ovarian reserve.

target.name: negative regulation of monocyte chemotaxis
target.description: Monocytes are recruited out of the bloodstream toward chemokine gradients at sites of injury and infection, and this recruitment has to be damped as well as driven; damping it is what negative regulation of monocyte chemotaxis does. Restraining monocyte influx limits the tissue damage of prolonged inflammation and shapes how atherosclerotic lesions, fibrotic scars and healing wounds develop, since each depends on how many monocyte-derived macrophages arrive.

members: [untitled BTM module] A mixed immune-expression module centred on mononuclear leukocyte identity and trafficking, combining chemokine receptors, GTPase-of-immunity-associated proteins and transcriptional regulators. Monocyte and macrophage recruitment to inflamed tissue depends on CCR2 and CX3CR1, whose ligands direct patrolling and infiltrating cells to vessel walls and injured sites; loss of this axis blunts inflammatory monocyte egress from bone marrow and reshapes atherosclerotic and neuroinflammatory disease.

[untitled BTM module] Circulating monocytes find their way into tissue by reading chemokine gradients, and the two receptors that anchor this group, CCR2 and CX3CR1, are the pair that defines the classical and non-classical monocyte subsets and governs their recruitment to inflamed vessel walls, injured tissue and the brain, where they become macrophages or microglia. Loss or blockade of this axis limits atherosclerotic plaque myeloid influx and blunts inflammatory infiltration, which is why it is a longstanding drug target.

Matrix and matrix-associated products such as tenascin C, ECM2, OLFML3 and the BMP antagonist chordin-like 1 shape tissue architecture and the diffusion of morphogens, while locally produced complement components C1S and C7 give stroma a role in innate immune surveillance.

[untitled BTM module] These genes read as the secretory programme of a mesenchymal stromal or fibroblast-like cell that builds and maintains tissue architecture and supports the cells embedded in it. [untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on membrane traffic through the Golgi and the machinery that buds, tethers and fuses transport vesicles, the route by which secretory and lysosomal cargo reaches its destination. Its outputs are secretion, receptor recycling and delivery of hydrolases such as cathepsin D to lysosomes; when it falters, cargo is mislocalised and organelle identity degrades.

[untitled BTM module] Membrane traffic and organelle remodelling form the common thread here: newly folded cargo leaves the endoplasmic reticulum in COPII-coated vesicles built from SEC23A and SEC24B, is delivered through early endosomes marked by the tethering factor EEA1, and reaches the plasma membrane by SNARE-directed fusion, with STXBP3 acting among the Sec1/Munc18-family regulators of that step. Lipid composition and cytoskeletal geometry are managed alongside cargo flow: the inositol phosphatase SYNJ1 dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 to uncoat vesicles after endocytosis, TMEM30A serves as the accessory subunit that allows P4-ATPase flippases to translocate aminophospholipids across bilayers, and the microtubule-severing ATPase SPAST shapes tubules and axonal microtubule arrays.

[untitled BTM module] Membrane traffic and organelle remodelling form the common thread here: newly folded cargo leaves the endoplasmic reticulum in COPII-coated vesicles built from SEC23A and SEC24B, is delivered through early endosomes marked by the tethering factor EEA1, and reaches the plasma membrane by SNARE-directed fusion, with STXBP3 acting among the Sec1/Munc18-family regulators of that step. Lipid composition and cytoskeletal geometry are managed alongside cargo flow: the inositol phosphatase SYNJ1 dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 to uncoat vesicles after endocytosis, TMEM30A serves as the accessory subunit that allows P4-ATPase flippases to translocate aminophospholipids across bilayers, and the microtubule-severing ATPase SPAST shapes tubules and axonal microtubule arrays.

target.name: regulation of removal of superoxide radicals
target.description: Superoxide generated by respiration, NADPH oxidases and uncoupled nitric oxide synthase must be disposed of quickly, and this pathway covers the control layer that sets how fast that clearance happens rather than the dismutation chemistry itself. Tuning it matters for vascular tone and endothelial health: when superoxide removal lags, nitric oxide is consumed to form peroxynitrite, signalling is distorted and oxidative damage accumulates.
